02Inspect the geometry

Revision 4: correct the lower bow contour

The previous hull keel rose while the bulb underside dipped. Their intersection and the wide smooth union produced the visible bump. Isolated field checks and guide fairing did not detect this defect.

The hull and bulb now share a lower curve through the aft join. A narrow blend starts gradually at the bulb root. It increases near the forward stem. The lower curve returns gradually to the existing rounded tip.

These measurements test the sampled contours; they do not prove global curvature continuity.

The saved model passed all 17 native field checks. The report uses the corrected notebook's native views. This work improves the visible shape. It does not establish a hydrodynamic optimum or a 99% reference match.

04The loft remains editable

The hull uses three shared longitudinal spline guides: half breadth, deck sheer, and keel height. A transverse cubic spline follows these guides along the hull. A conic loft forms the bulbous bow. Its upper and lower rails set the center and height. The hull and bulb share the lower rail at the aft join. A native spherical cap rounds the tip.

Clipping fields close the deck and hull ends. Native plane intersections form the faceted deckhouses. Separate display groups apply the hull, waterline, deck, and glazing colors.

These methods follow the previous F16 and Lockheed A-12 loft work. The controls below describe this reconstruction, with the stern at x = 0 and the bow at x = 1.

Acceptance method

Silhouette intersection over union equals the common mask area divided by the combined mask area. Each view must reach 0.99 against an independent source mask. The current model has no such score.

Use a common 3D scale, documented orthographic cameras, and fixed image thresholds. Do not change reference masks to improve the score. A high silhouette score alone does not validate hidden geometry or dimensions.

The saved graph reports 2,527 nodes and no recorded block errors. The report uses 10 native renders. API import time: 208.75 seconds, measured on this build.
